title: Cincinnati Bengals vs. Baltimore Ravens Postgame Analysis: What Happened, What We Got Right and What We Learned
seo_title: Cincinnati Bengals 35-13 Baltimore Ravens: EdgeDesk Postgame Thesis Audit
excerpt: Cincinnati Bengals won 35-13. The number did not land and the reasoning half held. There is something here to investigate without concluding the model is broken.
seo_description: Cincinnati Bengals beat Baltimore Ravens 35-13. EdgeDesk’s number implied Baltimore Ravens +4 — loss. 3 of 11 gradeable claims held up, 3 did not. Process grade: MIXED. Research, not picks.
model_status_note: The number did not land and the reasoning half held. There is something here to investigate without concluding the model is broken.
author: EdgeDesk Research
research_source: Ratings: EdgeDesk’s NFL rating state — trained seeds through 2025 plus 94 absorbed 2026 games, opponent-adjusted from the public nflverse team-week feed. Projection: the same edgedesk_football_v1.0.0 call the game card makes. Nothing on this page was computed in your browser twice.
market_source: The sportsbook number on this page is a quote EdgeDesk captured at Caesars and DraftKings on 2026-09-13, replayed from a committed snapshot rather than read live. It is the book’s number, not EdgeDesk’s, and EdgeDesk’s own number was produced before it was read. Source: EdgeDesk odds capture (public.signals), read by the newsletter pipeline.

EdgeDesk projected a away margin of 1.9 and the game finished 22 the away way — 20.1 points of margin error, OUTSIDE the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 22-point margin
variance_markers.text: Once a game is this far apart both teams stop playing the game they were rated on — the leader runs clock, the trailer throws — so late-game rates describe the situation rather than either team.

verdict.line: The number did not land and the reasoning half held. There is something here to investigate without concluding the model is broken.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 3 of the claims in this article rested on model, home_field.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; home advantage is priced into the number and cannot be isolated from one game’s box score..
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, home_field.

lessons.pregame_expectation: The model published an outcome range of -18.0 → +17.0 (Baltimore Ravens).
lessons.actual_result: The game finished outside it, at a margin of 22.
lessons.lesson: The published range is meant to contain eight results in ten. A miss is expected roughly twice in ten games and is only a problem in aggregate — which is exactly what this store exists to measure.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Count range misses across the season. A rate materially above 20% means the model’s stated uncertainty is too narrow.
